name: mcp-host
description: Expert prior for an MCP host (Claude, Cursor or any Model Context Protocol client) answering a question from Synapse with the synapse_* tools. Its ACTION nodes are those tool names, so the host's own tool calls localise it on the graph; graphrag-navigator is the backend navigator's own graph, whose actions are the navigator's internal tools. Hand-designed as the starting point (G0). Structure after Lu, Chen, Wu, Arık, 'Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents', arXiv:2609.09153.

nodes.description: A question about the user's documents has been received and no Synapse tool has been called yet.
Classify the question before calling a tool: about specific entities or facts, a thematic overview of the corpus, or the knowledge graph itself; and decide what a complete answer must contain.

Retrieve budgeted GraphRAG context for a question (context, citations, reasoning paths, source excerpts and usage) without generating an answer; embedding and graph queries only, no LLM call on the backend.
Find entities whose name or type contains a substring; returns the labels the graph actually uses, with their types, descriptions and degree.
List the corpus' themes: community titles and summaries, largest first.
Size and shape of the knowledge graph: node and edge counts, entities and relationships per type, and the best-connected entities.
Diagnose the backend: liveness, readiness, whether Neo4j is up, its version and its providers.
Get the backend's own generated answer with citations and sources; costs a second LLM call on top of the host's.
Check every claim of the draft answer against the returned context, citations, reasoning paths and source excerpts, and note whether the context was truncated.
Write the final answer from the verified context only, citing the entity names relied on, and say plainly what the graph does not contain.
The answer, or the reason there is none, has been given; the run is over.

edges.guidance: Before calling any Synapse tool, decide what the question needs: facts about named entities or their relationships, a thematic overview of the documents, or facts about the knowledge graph itself; and what a complete answer must contain.
edges.pitfalls: Do not answer from your own knowledge: the user is asking about their documents, so every claim must come from what Synapse returns.

edges.condition: When the question asks about specific entities, facts or relationships in the documents (the usual case)
edges.guidance: Start with synapse_retrieve under a budget: the question as query, k=8 (up to 12 for a broad question) and the default max_context_chars, lowered when tokens are scarce. It makes no backend LLM call, and identical calls are served from a cache.
edges.pitfalls: Do not start with synapse_ask: it bills a second LLM call for an answer you can write yourself from the retrieved context. Do not raise max_context_chars before the default budget has proven too small.

edges.condition: When the question names an entity whose exact label in the graph is uncertain (an abbreviation, a partial name or an alternative spelling)
edges.guidance: Call synapse_find_entities with the shortest distinctive fragment of the name (a surname, a key word) to learn the label the graph uses before retrieving.
edges.pitfalls: It is a substring match over names and types, not a search engine: a whole sentence matches nothing, and an empty result does not prove the entity is absent.

edges.condition: When the question is thematic or global: what the documents are about, their main topics, or a summary across the whole corpus
edges.guidance: Call synapse_communities once to read the corpus' themes (titles and summaries, largest first) and pick the ones the question is about.
edges.pitfalls: Community summaries are overviews written at ingestion time, not evidence: a concrete claim still needs an entity or a source excerpt from synapse_retrieve.

edges.condition: When the question is about the knowledge graph itself (its size, entity or relationship types, best-connected entities) or you need to know whether anything has been ingested
edges.guidance: Call synapse_graph_stats; it makes no LLM call, and its counts and per-type breakdowns answer questions about the graph directly.
edges.pitfalls: Do not call it before every question: it describes the graph, not the answer to a question about the documents.

edges.condition: When Synapse tools failed earlier in the conversation (backend unreachable, HTTP error) or the user asks whether Synapse is running
edges.guidance: Call synapse_status to see whether the backend is live and ready and whether Neo4j is up before retrying anything.
edges.pitfalls: Do not call it as a routine first step; it only diagnoses failures.

edges.condition: Only when the user explicitly asks for Synapse's own generated answer
edges.guidance: Call synapse_ask with the question; it returns the backend's grounded answer with its citations, reasoning paths and sources.
edges.pitfalls: Never call synapse_ask by default, to double-check, or to save writing: every call bills a second LLM generation on top of yours, while synapse_retrieve returns the same evidence without one.

edges.condition: When the backend reports healthy and ready with Neo4j up
edges.guidance: The backend is fine, so the earlier failure came from the request: retry synapse_retrieve once with a shorter query or the default budget.
edges.pitfalls: Do not retry the same failing call in a loop; if it fails again, report its error message to the user.

edges.condition: When the backend is unreachable, not ready, or reports Neo4j down
edges.guidance: Tell the user Synapse is unavailable, quote what synapse_status reported, and stop.
edges.pitfalls: Do not fall back to answering from your own knowledge as if it came from the user's documents.

edges.guidance: Retrieve with the question rewritten to use the entity label exactly as synapse_find_entities returned it; if several labels match, take the one whose type fits the question (the best-connected one when in doubt). If nothing matched even a short fragment, retrieve with the question as written: retrieval matches by meaning, not spelling.
edges.pitfalls: Do not answer from the entity list: labels, types and short descriptions are pointers to evidence, not evidence.

edges.condition: When the answer needs concrete evidence behind a theme (a name, a number, a date or a claim)
edges.guidance: Retrieve with the theme's key terms plus the question's focus (k=12 for a broad topic), one retrieval per theme you need evidence on.
edges.pitfalls: Do not call synapse_communities again for each sub-question; the theme list does not change within a task.

edges.condition: When the question only asks what the documents are about and the titles and summaries answer it
edges.guidance: Check that each theme you will name appears in the returned titles or summaries, and keep the largest themes first.
edges.pitfalls: Do not present a summary's wording as a quoted fact from a document.

edges.condition: When the graph holds entities of the kinds the question is about
edges.guidance: Retrieve with the question; the top entities and entity types in the stats suggest which labels to use in the query.
edges.pitfalls: Do not retrieve from an empty graph: with zero nodes there is nothing to find, so report that instead.

edges.condition: When the question is about the graph itself, or the graph is empty
edges.guidance: Answer with the counts and per-type breakdowns exactly as returned; for an empty graph, say nothing has been ingested yet and that documents can be added with synapse_ingest_pdf.
edges.pitfalls: The counts describe what was extracted from the ingested documents, not the world; do not present them as facts about the domain.

edges.guidance: Draft the answer from the returned context only, then check each claim against the citations, reasoning paths and source excerpts. Read usage.truncated: when it is true, the context was cut to the budget.
edges.pitfalls: Do not fill a gap with outside knowledge. If the context misses what the question needs, retrieve again with a narrower query (or a larger max_context_chars when usage.truncated is true), or resolve the name with synapse_find_entities, at most twice more. If the call returned an error, call synapse_status before retrying.

edges.guidance: Check the generated answer against its own citations and source excerpts before relaying it, and relay it with those citations.
edges.pitfalls: Do not pass the answer on as verified when its sources do not state it; the backend's model can be wrong too. Do not call synapse_ask again just to rephrase it.

edges.condition: When every claim you will make is supported by what Synapse returned, or you have established what the graph does not contain
edges.guidance: Write the answer from the verified context only, cite the entity names you relied on, mention a reasoning path when it connects the answer, and say plainly which parts the graph does not contain. Then record the run.
edges.pitfalls: Do not present a partial answer as complete: when usage.truncated was true or a part is unsupported, say so. Never guess to fill a gap.

edges.guidance: After answering, record the run with synapse_record_trajectory: the question, every Synapse call as [{action, observation}] and an honest score in [0, 1].
edges.pitfalls: Never inflate the score: 1 only when the answer is complete and supported by the graph, 0 when it failed. Do not call more Synapse tools after answering.
